how: Repeated members start flag proposals and recruitment, without one demonstrated founder controlling the subsequent attempts.
Calls repeatedly recruit members to make a flag and supply changing targets and coordinates.
A volunteer answers a night-duty call with a short commitment reframed as daytime duty abroad.
Members compare weak participation with other communities while disputing whether numbers, ordinary activities or the effort's importance explain it.
Explaining the canvas rules and neighbouring work makes participation intelligible, a sensemaking process represented on the ladder but unnamed among the standing processes.
Starting and recruiting can occur in the same proposal, so a separate starter-then-call sequence must not be inferred from these concepts.
Coordinates supplied within a recruitment thread receive a direct report of placing one square, grounding a local route from the call into building.
A guard call receives a bare written acceptance, but this pair cannot establish obligations for silent readers or a general distribution of preferred responses.
Too few hands can justify retaining a smaller existing heart, without establishing that all defenders stopped fighting or moved to a new site.
Builders select and revise a national flag through stripe conversion, lettering, a smaller heart and a later plan below a neighbour.
Members report partial progress and individual placing while coordinating borders and the flag's location.
Coordinates, sketches, a named main plan and a reposted skyline guide where and how helpers should place.
Published plans coordinate only helpers who encounter and recognise them, as apologies attribute friendly erasure to missing the plan or mistaking it for vandalism.
An autorepair request and script provision establish available automation rather than successful execution, while an unlimited-tile glitch remains a participant claim.
One room cannot test cross-room prevalence, and plan selection plus proposed guard duty cannot establish either formal command or the absence of other organising decisions.
A posted template does not settle coordination unless placers recognise it, because replies to the skyline plan admit erasing its intended changes.
Maintenance combines heart protection, defence calls, direct messages to overwriters and requested night coverage.
Helpers identify their own erased pixels as friendly interference caused by not seeing the plan or mistaking planned work for vandalism.
The completion post receives a maintenance request reporting a repaired black pixel, connecting an achieved part with something participants now seek to keep.
Maintenance produces an autorepair request and a supplied script, but neither successful machine placing nor a manpower shortfall causing adoption is established.
Members negotiate named territorial conflicts through messages, truce announcements and permission requests, without every reported agreement having an evidenced outcome.
Individuals carry conflict-solving messages to another subreddit and plead in a chat for nearby space, showing emissary work without proving formal delegation.
Reported overwriting by a named neighbour is met with a message explicitly intended to solve that conflict.
Members urge peaceful flag building, permission rather than vandalism, and negotiation instead of covering a neighbour's artwork.
Restraint appeals and truce announcements do not demonstrate agreed boundaries securing compliance, particularly when a later neighbour reports its work destroyed.
A neighbour volunteers help, receives thanks after repeated losses, and later becomes the object of a reciprocal repair request.
A reply explicitly welcomes neighbouring help because earlier flag attempts were repeatedly hijacked.
A heart plan intended for both subreddits and a later shared-heart announcement establish a joint-mark arrangement without demonstrating broader coalition administration.
The arriving helper cites seeing construction, while the joint-heart plan appears later, leaving a prior border bargain as the cause of help unobserved.
Defence calls and a joint mark occur, but the cited record does not connect coalition formation to a shared threat.
Visible construction can attract unsolicited neighbouring help before an evidenced bargain, because the visitor explicitly says seeing the flag prompted help.
An offer arriving after placement closes establishes willingness in talk, without establishing possible assistance on that closed canvas.
A request to rebuild inside the flag establishes proposed hosting, while redirection and competing loyalty leave approval, occupancy and restoration unresolved.
A visitor demands a diplomat over encroachment, supporting the minimal representative-request form while internal disagreement over binding authority remains unobserved.
The demand for a representative is explicitly grounded in an invading flag rather than an evidenced dispute about compliance with a concluded agreement.
Claimed encroachment can prompt a demand for a diplomatic representative without an intervening agreement whose authority is contested.
Members propose relocation or a smaller heart after competing work and invasion make earlier flag plans untenable.
Losses ground a new site proposal and precede a later account of building finally taking off, supporting a local restart sequence without an inevitable rebuilding loop.
Nation-building jokes and National Service language frame the work, while a participant explicitly ranks national loyalty above affection for a neighbouring fandom.
Haze complaints from outside the canvas enter jokes about the neighbour taking the heart and changing the flag, without establishing why attacks were initiated.
Haze jokes narrate loss and defence, while the cited attack calls do not identify haze as their reason, leaving inherited friction as attack motivation unobserved.
Members perform, recognise and evaluate April Fools jokes before and alongside canvas work, while another theme proposes a future subreddit disguise rather than enacting it.
Members and moderators redirect duplicates into a sticky and later request its removal to restore an ordinary university thread.
A takeover call receives a moderator's direction to stop new threads and use the pinned one, demonstrating a local response rather than measuring a room-wide flood.
Centralising coordination includes replacing an abandoned sticky and renewing its main plan, rather than merely gathering posts into one permanent thread.
Celebration can announce an achievement that contemporaries deny ever existed, so the ritual must be distinguished from verified completion and from a later separate build.
A celebration cannot certify its preceding achieved state when replies deny the flag was ever whole, while the later attempt has its own attributed completion account.
Members record immediate loss, dispute the claimed state and mark the canvas ending, rather than documenting only successful work retrospectively.
Celebration elicits competing accounts of what existed, making correction and disagreement part of recording rather than assuming preservation of an agreed completed achievement.
The strongest version disputes precede placement's end, while the ending report does not establish a later cleanup dispute or contest over a preserved copy.
Closing a sticky and proposing next year's subreddit disguise do not establish a decision to continue the canvas collective or carry its work elsewhere.
An ending report and an unsticky request do not connect recording to a decision about preserving the mark, adopting it or continuing on another canvas.
Recruitment explicitly includes hijacking flags and converting existing stripes into the proposed national mark.
The contest continues in haze jokes and a post-close challenge to a visitor's claims, rather than ending with placement.
A recruitment proposal can itself call for conversion of a rival flag, without a separately observed turn from neutral construction to attack.
A takeover proposal receives a question about inciting war, showing an objection without establishing effective restraint or a general pattern of reason-giving refusals.
Takeover calls coexist with peace requests and a truce announcement, but the coded passages do not establish that a specific call caused that truce.
A haze joke answers a defence call about the flag being changed, so contest talk can follow being attacked rather than the room's own attack.
